Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — the platform looks promising. Procurement has a few gating items before we can issue a formal PO and map invoices into our weekly payment run:

- PO format: Our AP system needs a PO with a specific fields block (Entity Code, BU Code, Cost Center, Project Tag). Can you confirm Redwood will accept a PO that includes those?
- Net terms: We typically run Net60 for platforms of this size. Is Net60 on the table for Orchid? If not, what flexibility exists if we commit to a 12-month volume?
- Invoice cadence: We prefer a weekly statement (cutoff Friday) that aggregates usage. Any chance Redwood can support a weekly invoice lane for committed customers?
- Pre-auth / early invoice: For initial onboarding we sometimes need a pre-auth or deposit invoice to reserve capacity. Can Redwood issue a single pre-auth invoice and then regular weekly usage invoices?

Can you loop in whoever owns billing/finance at Redwood if helpful. AP copied here will need the PO template to get it through our ERP.

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can draft the PO and SOW.

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear list. Tagging Vanessa (billing) and Karthik (sales ops) to confirm process details. Quick answers up front:

- PO fields: Yes, we can accept a PO that includes Entity Code, BU Code, Cost Center and Project Tag. We ask for the PO number to live in the "PO/Ref" header field on invoices so our ERP can match automatically.
- Net terms: Standard hosted customers default to Net30. We can offer Net60 on 12‑month committed plans with a small prepayment or a credit holdback (depends on billing volume). If Orchid can commit to a monthly minimum, we can extend Net60 — details below.
- Invoice cadence: Weekly aggregated statements are supported for customers on committed plans; we can set a Friday cutoff and produce a single weekly statement.
- Pre-auth / early invoice: We can issue a one-time pre-auth invoice or an advance credit invoice to reserve capacity and apply it against weekly usage.

I'll attach a short pricing summary and our PO template. Vanessa / Karthik, can you confirm the minimum monthly commitment threshold for Net60 and the mechanics for a pre-auth credit?

Next steps: Megan — if you can share Orchid's required PO template fields (or the ERP export format), we'll populate our template and return a redline for your AP. Meanwhile I'll outline two options for Net60 in the attached pricing summary.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Megan — Vanessa from Billing here. Thanks for laying this out. A few operational clarifications and the proposed approach: 

1) PO field mapping and PO/Ref: Please include the following exact fields on the PO PDF/ERP export so our system maps cleanly: PO Number (PO/Ref), Entity Code, BU Code, Cost Center, Project Tag, Invoice Delivery Email (or AP endpoint). If your ERP can include a CSV export of those fields, we can ingest programmatically.

2) Net60 parameters: We can offer Net60 if Orchid signs a 12‑month committed plan with a minimum monthly spend of $25k and either: (A) 25% prepayment applied to the first month, or (B) a 10% billing holdback released after 90 days. Option A shortens collections risk and is preferred for first-year pilots. We can include either in the SOW/invoice terms.

3) Weekly invoice lane: We will set a Friday cutoff, generate a consolidated weekly statement showing line‑item usage and token counts, and attach a CSV for ERP reconciliation. Note: weekly statements require the commitment above to keep per‑invoice processing cost reasonable.

4) Pre-auth / advance credit: We can issue an advance credit invoice (labeled "Pre-Auth Reservation") for a one-time amount and track it on the account. That credit will be applied to weekly invoices until exhausted. The credit invoice is refundable per the contract terms in case of early termination.

5) PO / invoice naming and remittance: To avoid mismatches, please ensure the PO/Ref is present and that remittance instructions on our invoices match Orchid's AP routing. We can include Orchid's AP email in the invoice header as requested.

If those terms look okay, Ben and I will draft a short SOW clause and update the PO template with exact field mapping. Megan — would AP be able to supply a sample PO export (PDF or CSV) so we can validate the mapping?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
